newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia truck strike blocks 21,000 bags coffee.
newsitem.headline: Colombia truck strike blocks 21,000 bags coffee.

text.p: BOGOTA, Aug 19 Reuter - A strike by Colombian truck drivers in Colombia's main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura has blocked the export of about 21,000 60-kg bags of coffee, a truckers' leader said Monday.

About 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports are shipped out of Buenaventura. The strike began late Saturday but passed virtually unnoticed given that it came during a three-day bank holiday weekend.

"No trucks are going in or out of the port. We have about 3,000 trucks immobilized in and around Buenaventura and about 30 of them are loaded with about 700 bags each of coffee," Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC told Reuters.
The ACC declared the strike in protest at transport companies' failure to increase freight rates in line with an accord hammered out at the end of a strike in April.

The ACC is demanding that a Transport Ministry representative attends talks in Buenaventura to force transport companies to increase freight rates. If there is no agreement in the next 24 hours, Suarez said the ACC, which represents about 85 percent of the country's truckers, could extend its action to Colombia's Atlantic coast ports.
Some sugar exports are also blocked by the strike action but Suarez as unable to say exactly how much.
